html:
A Quechua nobleman from the Andes of Peru who wrote and drew a long chronicle protesting Spanish rule, finished around 1615. He was born after the Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire and died some time after 1616.

He worked for colonial officials and priests and learned Spanish, and saw how Andean people were treated. His book, The First New Chronicle and Good Government, runs to nearly 1,200 pages, nearly 400 of them full page ink drawings. It covers:

  • Andean history before the Inca and the Inca kings and queens
  • the farming year, festivals, laws and roads of the Inca state
  • the abuses of Spanish officials, priests and landowners against Andean people

He addressed it as a letter to King Philip III of Spain, asking for reform. The king never saw it. The manuscript ended up in the Royal Library in Copenhagen and was only found in 1908. Its drawings are now among the main pictures we have of Inca life, alongside the words of Inca Garcilaso de la Vega.
